title: Emrys and the Salt
premise: Ines Vane, a mercenary bound by oath to a god who fell silent a decade ago, keeps the ledgers of the Salt Guild, which trades in impossible things: borrowed years, bottled grief, names. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin answering themselves across the city of Corvane, Ines discovers her silent god is awake too — and that it has been feeding on the souls its faithful sold in desperation, including the soul of Tam, the guild's youngest runner and Ines's found-family anchor. To steal Tam back from the court beneath the mountain, Ines must break her own oath, unmake the ledger she has spent years perfecting, and confront the truth that her god chose silence not from death but from greed. She succeeds at terrible cost: the god dies, the ledgers burn, and Ines — stripped of the identity her oath gave her — chooses to remain with her ragged found family, keeping only an ordinary book in which she writes down what must be remembered.
about_author: E. M. Nakamura is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing debt records in port cities before turning to fiction. They write about oaths, ledgers, and the people who keep both.

chapters.title: The Weight of Entries
chapters.summary: Ines Vane audits the Salt Guild's winter ledgers, establishing her precision, her silence-sworn faith, and her fierce protectiveness of Tam, a runner who sells a year of his life to pay his sister's debt. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: quiet devotion disguised as bureaucracy; the first crack shows when a prayer Ines mutters goes unanswered as always.

chapters.title: What the Bells Heard
chapters.summary: Across Corvane, answered prayers begin causing small miracles and small disasters; the guild scrambles to price the impossible. Ines witnesses a drowned child walk out of the river alive. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as she realizes the old gods are moving, and hers may be among them.

chapters.title: A Contract in Ash
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Ossa reveals a sealed contract from decades past: desperate faithful sold their souls to the Silent God for miracles, payment deferred until the god woke. Tam's grandmother was one such seller — and the debt passed down. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: betrayal; the ledger she trusted contains a horror she helped preserve.

chapters.title: Tam, Running
chapters.summary: Tam begins sleepwalking toward the mountain, his body answering a summons he doesn't understand. Ines ties him to her wrist with a salt-cord and lies to him about why. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: fear and stubborn cheer; he trusts Ines completely, which makes her lie unbearable.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Ines descends into old mining warrens where the Silent God's court convenes — masked servitors, a throne of fused prayer-stones. She sees soul-ledgers older than the guild's. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: awe and violation; her god is not dead but hoarding, and she recognizes its handwriting because it matches her own training.

chapters.title: Price of Passage
chapters.summary: To move freely below, Ines trades the guild an impossible thing of her own: her memory of the day she took her oath. The guild accepts. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: grief for something she can no longer miss; the theme of memory-as-identity made literal.

chapters.title: Ossa's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Ossa argues the pragmatic path: let Tam go, honor the contract, protect the guild. Ines refuses and is formally struck from the rolls. POV: Ossa. Emotional beat: cold sorrow between two people who respect each other; found family fractures along the fault line of survival versus loyalty.

chapters.title: Salt and Iron
chapters.summary: Ines recruits allies: Brannoc, a disgraced priest whose god also woke and rejected him, and Sefa, a thief who once stole a year of her own life back. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: wary hope; a found family assembling itself out of the discarded.

chapters.title: The Night of Small Miracles
chapters.summary: Answered prayers spike citywide; temples overflow; riots begin as gods grant wishes carelessly. Ines realizes the waking gods are starving, consuming worship like meat. POV: Brannoc. Emotional beat: disillusioned fury; he prayed twenty years for this and got a god that doesn't know his name.

chapters.title: What Ines Forgot
chapters.summary: Sefa recovers the pawned memory from the guild vaults but Ines cannot safely reabsorb it yet. Reading her own recorded oath, she learns her god demanded she forget everyone she loved before swearing. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: vertigo; her entire identity was curated by the thing she serves.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: The three descend through collapsing warrens as the mountain shudders with the god's feeding. Tam's summons accelerates; they race his sleepwalking body downward. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve; Tam chooses to walk toward the throne awake rather than be dragged.

chapters.title: The Tollgate of Names
chapters.summary: A servitor gate demands each traveler surrender a true name. Sefa gives a stolen one; Brannoc gives his god's secret name; Ines gives nothing and cuts through instead. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: gallows humor over an abyss; the cost of passage is becoming literal.

chapters.title: Audience with Silence
chapters.summary: Ines stands before the Silent God, which speaks for the first time in a decade — offering to restore her memories, forgive Tam, and return her oath if she brings it more souls. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: temptation rendered as tenderness; the god knows exactly how to sound like family.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Ines refuses, and the god takes Tam's soul into the throne of prayer-stones to force her hand. Brannoc and Sefa hold the court's servitors at the doors. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: heartbreak hardening into war; she declares the contract void and prepares to unwrite it.

chapters.title: Ledger-Breaker
chapters.summary: Ines fights her way to the court's master ledger, discovering her own oath-page is the binding clause that empowers the whole book. To destroy it, she must destroy the self it wrote. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the climax of identity; she chooses the people over the person.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Answer
chapters.summary: As servitors breach the doors, Brannoc calls his own waking god by its secret name and commands it to look at him — and it does, briefly, before the distraction costs him dearly. POV: Brannoc. Emotional beat: bitter grace; he gets one moment of being seen, and spends it buying his friends time.

chapters.title: The Unwriting
chapters.summary: Ines tears her oath-page free and burns it in the throne's flame; the master ledger unravels, souls pour loose, and the Silent God screams in a voice made of every prayer it ever ignored. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: cathartic destruction; ten years of silence ending in noise.

chapters.title: Tam, Returned
chapters.summary: Tam wakes on the mountainside with his soul restored but a year of borrowed time still missing. Ines, memoryless of her oath but not of him, cannot explain why she is crying. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: tender disorientation; love persisting without its reasons.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Gods
chapters.summary: Corvane reckons with fading miracles and empty temples; Ossa reopens the guild under new rules forbidding soul-trade. He offers Ines her place back. POV: Ossa. Emotional beat: reconciliation without erasure; some debts are honored by changing the terms.

chapters.title: The Ordinary Book
chapters.summary: Ines buys a plain blank book with her last coin and begins writing down everything worth remembering: names, debts forgiven, recipes, jokes. Sefa and Brannoc move into rooms above her workshop. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: quiet rebuilding; identity chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Keeps
chapters.summary: Ines returns alone to the dead court and finds one prayer-stone still warm — her god's last fragment, whispering her forgotten memories as a final temptation. She leaves it there, unfed, and walks out into daylight. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: closure; some silences deserve to stay broken.

chapters.title: Entries, Continued
chapters.summary: A year later, the found family gathers for Tam's sister's wedding; Ines reads aloud from her ordinary book the record of everything they survived. The last entry is simply all their names. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: full-circle resolution; memory kept not by gods or ledgers but by the people who choose each other.
